provenance.scope: A2(2급) vocabulary reinforcement -- FIRST A2 batch in the C3 series -- 64 headwords (47 nouns, 10 verbs, 6 adjectives, 1 adverb) from the NIKL KIIQ 2017 grade-2 gap list (not yet live at any level, not in Batch 25-30's A1 drafts). Fills every currently under-12 live A2 pack to 12/12 (27 packs, 58 words) plus one new pack a2_messenger_phone_1 (6/12, partial -- see newPacks). Original clean-room authoring (KO/DE/EN), seeded only by NIKL 2017 kiiq grade-2 headword selection (KOGL Type-1) and docs/data/sejong/syllabus_sejong2.json unit topics for prioritization. Follows the persona (character_profiles.json recurringCharacters) rules, docs/CONTENT_LEVEL_BIBLE.md §B.2 (A2 sentence/grammar/vocabulary ceiling) and docs/CONTENT_PERSONA_VOICE.md (A2 반말 transitions / short idioms) set for this level.
provenance.seedSource: tools/content_factory/lexicon/nikl_kiiq_2017_vocab.csv (grade=2, minus live assets/data/korean_vocab.csv at ANY level, minus tools/content_factory/drafts/batch_25..30_a1_rows.csv); topic priority cross-referenced against docs/data/sejong/syllabus_sejong2.json (Sejong 2 = A2 unit vocabulary lists).
provenance.wordSourceNote: NIKL grade-2 headwords total 1087 unique strings (excluding bound affixes like -되다); removing everything already live at any level (A1-C2, 2562 rows) or present in the Batch 25-30 A1 drafts leaves a gap of 791 headwords -- this is the FIRST A2 batch against that gap, so 791-64=727 remain for future batches (comparable in scale to the 6-batch A1 reinforcement program, Batch 25-30). Selection order: (1) every live A2 pack with fewer than 12 words (27 packs, needing 58 words total to reach 12/12 each -- see packsFilledTo12) was filled FIRST, matching topic words to that pack's existing theme, prioritizing a citable docs/data/sejong/syllabus_sejong2.json unit's vocabulary list where a grade-2 match existed (15 words directly citable: 마치다/이사/빨래/쓰레기/버리다/닦다/돌리다 [unit5], 장마 [unit6], 메모/메시지 [unit7], 박수/자리 [unit11, ultimately not used -- see below], 새벽/자신 [units 12/14, not used], 소리 [unit13]); (2) the remaining 43 words were matched by topic to each pack's existing theme from the broader grade-2 gap list (docs/data/sejong/syllabus_sejong2.json's own vocabulary lists turned out to skew heavily toward grade 3-5 for several unit topics -- e.g. ALL of unit 4's taste adjectives [고소하다/느끼하다/달콤하다/새콤하다] and unit 9's emotion adjectives [기쁘다/무섭다/부끄럽다/즐겁다/지루하다/게으르다] are already grade-1/2 and already LIVE, so no new headwords were available there); (3) after all 27 packs reached 12/12, the remaining word-count budget (64-58=6) went to one NEW pack, a2_messenger_phone_1 (Kommunikation), built from 6 of the 15 Sejong-citable words that were not needed to fill an existing pack (휴대폰/메시지/메모/답장/연락처/끊다) -- matching the level bible's can-do list item '메신저로 소통하고'.
provenance.sejongCitationNote: Direct grade-2 headword hits from docs/data/sejong/syllabus_sejong2.json (candidate == a single token extracted from a unit's multi-word vocab entry): unit2 마치다/이사; unit5 빨래/쓰레기/버리다/닦다/돌리다; unit6 장마; unit7 메모/메시지; unit11 박수/자리; unit12 새벽; unit13 소리; unit14 자신 -- 15 total. Of these, 박수/자리/자신 were NOT used (the 17-word a2_messenger_phone_1 slot only needed 6, and 박수/자리/자신 don't share that pack's communication theme as cleanly as 휴대폰/답장/연락처/끊다 do) -- they remain in the grade-2 gap pool for a future batch. Most other Sejong-2 unit vocab (taste adjectives unit4, weather-extreme nouns unit6 apart from 장마, travel nouns unit8, phone-etiquette nouns unit7's 별표/우물 정자, personality adjectives unit10, tech-fault nouns unit13 apart from 소리, self-assessment adjectives unit14 apart from 마치다/자신) turned out to be grade 3-5 on inspection, not grade 2 -- confirming the Q-S report's finding (docs/data/sejong/REPORT_2026-09-16.md) that a Sejong-textbook unit's nominal level and a word's actual NIKL frequency grade frequently diverge; this batch used the NIKL grade as the authoritative ceiling, per docs/CONTENT_LEVEL_BIBLE.md §B.2, not the Sejong unit number.
provenance.tierNote: Cloze distractors: Tier A (37/64 items) = real semantically-clashing words of the same POS/form, chosen for a narrow-enough collocation that the swap reads as nonsense (nouns: a generic pool of 24 unrelated concrete/event nouns, each independently carrying the correct particle allomorph for its OWN batchim class per distractor_particle_mismatches; verbs/adjectives: another real verb/adjective conjugated to the SAME tense/ending). Tier B (27/64 items) = a bare dictionary-form verb (from the Batch 25-30 precedent's DICTIONARY_FORM_VERB_POOL) or a bare grammatical particle (BARE_PARTICLES), used whenever the sentence's predicate frame was judged too open for a real-word swap to reliably avoid a second valid sentence (existential/generic frames: 있어요/없어요/오다/왔어요/이에요-type slots) -- deliberately conservative for this FIRST A2 batch, since open-class A2 sentences often lack the narrow selectional restriction a closed-class function-word batch (Batch 30) could rely on; a hand read of all 64 items is in the review packet's evidence table.
provenance.grammarNote: All 64 examples pass the CefrLexicon-based grade>=3 scan (tools/content_factory/scan_grammar_level.py --level A2's own detector, reused directly by this batch's test) with zero flagged hits. A2(2급) grammar is used explicitly in several rows: -을게(요) (정리 '내가 할게', 걱정 '도와줄게요', 잡다 '잡아 놓을게요', 끊다 '끊을게요'), -지 말고 (화내다), -을래요 (배드민턴 '칠래요?'), -는 것 같다 (주문 '들어간 것 같아요'), -지만 (튼튼하다 '오래됐지만'), -아/어 놓다 (잡다), -는데 (메시지 '보냈는데'). One grade-3 short-fragment false-positive risk (-잖아, which GrammarIndex's own <=2-syllable anti-overmatch guard cannot structurally detect -- see scan_grammar_level.py's docstring) was manually caught by grepping the corpus for 잖아/뿐/만큼/대로/어도/어야/는다 during authoring and removed before this draft (a 깜짝 example originally read '깜짝 놀랐잖아!', rewritten to '나 정말 깜짝 놀랐어!').
provenance.vocabCeilingNote: docs/CONTENT_LEVEL_BIBLE.md §B.2 ⑤ allows <=1 word per sentence outside the 1-2급 vocabulary ceiling. Two sentences intentionally use exactly one such word: 기뻐하다's example uses 합격 (NIKL grade 3, 'passing an exam') and 메시지's example uses 확인 (NIKL grade 3, 'to check/confirm') -- both extremely common, independently justified single exceptions, verified via tools/content_factory/a2_draft_rules.py's helper-word scanner (NIKL grade<=2 union the ENTIRE live vocabulary at any level, since a word already taught anywhere in the app is a safe helper word) applied to all 64 rows with a documented allow-list of exactly these 2 rows.

posRules.noun_particle_fold_tier_a: 37 items where the cloze answer folds the headword with an alternating particle (이/가, 을/를, 은/는, 이에요/예요) or a real conjugated predicate; distractors are real words of the same batchim-independent particle-allomorph shape (nouns) or the same tense/ending (verbs/adjectives), each individually verified via distractor_rules.batchim_class / a1_draft_rules.distractor_particle_mismatches.
posRules.open_frame_tier_b: 27 items whose predicate frame (있어요/없어요/오다/이에요-type existential or generic slots) is judged too open for a same-shape real-word swap to guarantee no second valid sentence; distractors are a bare dictionary-form verb (2-3 of: 가다/오다/보다/읽다/쓰다/타다/입다/알다/모르다/돕다/팔다/고르다/빌리다/끝나다/다니다/먹다/마시다/자다) and/or a bare grammatical particle with no host (에서/에게/한테/으로/와/과/랑) -- a bare dictionary form or a floating particle can never complete a well-formed Korean sentence in that slot, guaranteeing D7 (never a second valid answer) regardless of how open the surrounding frame is. Mirrors the PREDICATE_SLOT_WAIVER/OPEN_SLOT_WAIVER technique from Batch 25-30 and cloze_distractor_rules.py, generalized here to noun-particle-fold slots (not just bare predicate slots) -- a Tier-B distractor never carries the slot's own particle, since that would require the pool word to be a real host noun, defeating the point of the waiver.
posRules.nhada_tier_a: 입학/취소 (Sino-Korean noun + 하다, answer = '입학했어요'/'취소했어요', which structurally reads as headword+'했어요' since 하다's past tense elides into the noun) are treated like ordinary verb Tier-A rows (same-ending real-verb distractors: 도와줬어요/빌렸어요/끝났어요), not the noun-particle-fold mechanic -- the distractors are unrelated verbs in the same tense, not a suffix-consistent fold of a DIFFERENT noun.

openerDistribution.note: No '와/아/음/네/좋아요' bare reaction openers and no '우리 같이' invitations were used in this batch's 64 examples -- the word list this round (household/feelings/weather/family/commerce nouns and verbs) did not naturally call for the invitation-opener pattern the way earlier scenario-style batches did; this is a design note, not a violation (the '<=6' woori-gachi cap and reaction-opener caps are upper bounds, not floors).
